page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Marginal notes in the right margin (section numbers 377, 378, 378 and Greek and Latin catchwords beside the lines). Signature "E 2" at the foot. Running head "FLOS XXII." at the top, page number "64" at top right.

main_text.p: stoliebantur[?] exemplo Macchabæorum: qui parva suorum manu numerosissimas Antiochorum, Epiphanis & Eupatoris, itemq; Demetrii, Syriæ Regum, eorumq; legatorum copias multoties olim profligarant; plurimis ex his non raro deletis, dextras eorum & gladios dirigente ipso Deo: sed quia non similes his fuerunt, qui orando divinam armaturam è cœlo tunc deportarant: ideo stulta & infelici hac κακοζηλία[?] sibi totiquē genti [illegible, ~8 letters] accersiverunt.

PHILIPPO Macedonum Regi penultimo quantum profuerit bellum, quod κακοζηλία incitatus superioris Philippi, Alexandri Magni patris, (qui & ipse multum negotii Atheniensibus olim fecerat, urbis libertati infensus) urbi Atticæ movit: magnis suis cladibus, à Romanis acceptis, est experrtus.377

ÆTOLI, qui bello Macedonico primo contra hunc Philippum socia cum Romanis junxerant arma; hoc debellato, offensi, quod non ex ipsorum arbitrio Macedonia Philippo esset ademta, ipsisque in belli præmium data: Antiochum in Romana impulerunt bella: atque ita irrequieti, sibi ipsis foveam foderunt. Eo namque victo, cum soli adversus Romanos & viribus impares, & omni auxilio destituti remansissent: ab his paulo post & ipsi domiti, imperata facere sunt coacti.378

Sic ergo Ætolos ambitio & vindictæ studium in exitium præcipites egit: ipsaque libertate, quam illibatam adversus dominationem Atheniensium & Spartanorum inter tot Græciæ civitates sibi retinuerant, tandem privavit. Adeo res misera est non solùm vindictæ cupiditas: sed & ambitio, & appetitio principatûs: ut cœlum ruere, dummodo magistratus adipiscantur, multi exoptent: quod Varro dixit apud Nonium.

In hæc & similia exempla, quorum totus orbis plenus est, intuentes Reges & Principes, cæterique, ad clavum Reipublicæ qui sedent; Spartam, quam nacti πολυπραγμοσύνην[?] sunt, hanc ornent: & juxta Siracidæ præceptum, c.3. μ[illegible, ~6 letters] quæ mandata ipsis sunt, sanctè cogitent: nec fiducia pro- priæ sapientiæ aut potentiæ res periculosas & non ne-Principibusfugienda

page.notes: Marginal numbers 377 and 378 stand beside the paragraphs and are section references. The right-margin Greek catchwords ("κακοζηλία", "πολυπραγμοσύνην") and the Greek at the end of the last paragraph are only partly legible; the bracketed Greek is marked illegible. The word "stoliebantur" at the top of the page is doubtful. The printed "experrtus" appears to be a printing error and is left as printed. The page number "64" and the running head are read from the scan with some uncertainty about the digits. The final line runs off the page and is a catchword-free end at the signature "E 2".
